adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the United States (Wikipedia) — Housing of transgender inmates by state
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) stating that as of January 2021 California is the one state that allows transgender people to be housed in prison according to their gender identity, while New Mexico is the one state with separate facilities reserved for transgender people only; the article's U.S. state map legend codes California under 'Allows transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity' and notes the same context that federal policy returned to assigned-sex-at-birth placement after January 2017 guidance was rescinded. Placement axis: identity-based housing within the general population, with no trans-only separate facility documented for California.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in California (Wikipedia) — Prison policy
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) whose prison policy coverage documents that in 2015 California became the first state to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates, and cites KPBS reporting (2015) on 'Transgender In Prison: How California's New Guidelines Will Be Implemented' — CDCR's operational guidelines governing transgender inmates. Thin on the housing axis: the article confirms the identity-based care and guidance posture but contains no explicit statement of a trans-only unit or segregation practice.

records.note: California's documented practice is gender-identity-based mainstream housing: per enwiki 'LGBTQ rights in the United States', as of January 2021 California is the only state allowing transgender prisoners to be housed according to their gender identity (map legend: 'Allows transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity'); no trans-only separate facility is documented for California (unlike New Mexico's reserved units). CDCR guidance on transgender inmates (2015, per KPBS) and first-in-nation state funding for gender-affirming surgery for trans inmates (2015, Norsworthy case) round out the identity-affirming posture; the record's base-lane notice that federal policy shifted back to birth-sex placement does not alter California's state-level rule.

adds.title: Colorado Department of Corrections (Wikipedia) — Transgender inmates section
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) whose 'Transgender inmates' section documents the state's actual placement practice: a 2019 class action on behalf of transgender women held in men's prisons alleged CDOC subjected them to sexual and physical violence and denied medically necessary care, and a court-approved 2024 consent decree in Denver District Court (Raven v. Polis) required CDOC to expand health care and create voluntary specialized housing — a 100-bed unit at the men's Sterling facility and an integration unit at the women's prison — and to pay about $2.1 million to roughly 400 class members without admitting liability. It also records a 2019 settlement (Lindsay Saunders-Velez, $170,000) over the safety of a transgender inmate held in a men's prison. Placement axis: no identity-based-housing statute; trans women were historically held in men's prisons, with relief achieved through litigation and consent decree rather than a baseline housing rule.

records.note: Colorado has no statute housing transgender prisoners by gender identity; the documented practice is that transgender women were held in men's prisons under CDOC, remedied only through litigation: a 2019 $170,000 settlement (Saunders-Velez) over the safety of a transgender inmate in a men's prison, a 2019 class action alleging sexual/physical violence and denial of medically necessary care, and a 2024 Denver District Court consent decree (Raven v. Polis) requiring CDOC to expand health care and create voluntary specialized housing (100-bed unit at the men's Sterling facility, integration unit at the women's prison), with about $2.1 million paid to roughly 400 class members. Mainstream housing follows birth-sex assignment unless modified by consent-decree/voluntary units — the opposite of California's identity-based baseline.
